verses.text: For I desire to have you know how greatly I struggle for you, and for those at Laodicea, and for as many as have not seen my face in the flesh;

that their hearts may be comforted, they being knit together in love, and gaining all riches of the full assurance of understanding, that they may know the mystery of God, both of the Father and of Christ,
in whom are all the treasures of wisdom and knowledge hidden.
Now this I say that no one may delude you with persuasiveness of speech.
For though I am absent in the flesh, yet am I with you in the spirit, rejoicing and seeing your order, and the steadfastness of your faith in Christ.
As therefore you received Christ Jesus, the Lord, walk in him,
rooted and built up in him, and established in the faith, even as you were taught, abounding in it in thanksgiving.
Be careful that you don’t let anyone rob you through his philosophy and vain deceit, after the tradition of men, after the elements of the world, and not after Christ.
For in him all the fullness of the Godhead dwells bodily,
and in him you are made full, who is the head of all principality and power;
in whom you were also circumcised with a circumcision not made with hands, in the putting off of the body of the sins of the flesh, in the circumcision of Christ;
having been buried with him in baptism, in which you were also raised with him through faith in the working of God, who raised him from the dead.
You were dead through your trespasses and the uncircumcision of your flesh. He made you alive together with him, having forgiven us all our trespasses,
wiping out the handwriting in ordinances which was against us; and he has taken it out of the way, nailing it to the cross;
having stripped the principalities and the powers, he made a show of them openly, triumphing over them in it.
Let no one therefore judge you in eating, or in drinking, or with respect to a feast day or a new moon or a Sabbath day,
which are a shadow of the things to come; but the body is Christ’s.
Let no one rob you of your prize by a voluntary humility and worshiping of the angels, dwelling in the things which he has not seen, vainly puffed up by his fleshly mind,
and not holding firmly to the Head, from whom all the body, being supplied and knit together through the joints and ligaments, grows with God’s growth.
If you died with Christ from the elements of the world, why, as though living in the world, do you subject yourselves to ordinances,
“Don’t handle, nor taste, nor touch”
(all of which perish with use), according to the precepts and doctrines of men?
Which things indeed appear like wisdom in self-imposed worship, and humility, and severity to the body; but aren’t of any value against the indulgence of the flesh.

footnotes.content: Paul is miles away, yet his heart strains with prayer for these new believers he has never met face-to-face. This is what real shepherding looks like—not presence, but persistence in intercession. Even when we can't see someone in person, the Lord can see their heart, and our faithful struggle on their behalf matters.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Notice what Paul asks for his people: hearts comforted, love binding them together, understanding rich and full. He knows the deepest comfort isn't found in rules or certainties, but in knowing the Mystery—that Jesus is the fullness of God, hiding nothing from those who draw near. That's the treasure he wants them to hold.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Hidden treasures—not kept from us, but kept safe for us. In Christ all wisdom and knowledge lie concealed, like a lamp hidden but burning steady in darkness. The more we know Him, the more we discover we've been rich all along. Simple as that.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Paul cuts straight to the danger: clever words without Christ behind them. The world is full of smooth talkers and confident philosophies. His warning isn't fearful—it's a steady hand: stay rooted in reality, and the counterfeit won't fool you.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Though imprisoned far away, Paul's spirit is present with them, watching their faith hold firm like a fortress. He sees their order—their steadiness—and it gladdens him. Even when leaders cannot walk beside us, Christ walks with us, and He knows the faithful stand.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: You received Christ as Lord—now walk in Him. Not a moment's decision alone, but a lifetime's direction. Walking means trusting each day as you did on the first day: this is how you belong to Him.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Rooted and built up—a plant and a building at once. His growth is dual: roots going down into Christ, strength rising up in faith. Thanksgiving is the air of this life; it's how we know we're growing true.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Robbers use fine words and borrowed wisdom—the tradition of men, the elements of the world—to steal your prize. But you have Christ, the real treasure. Guard what the Lord has given you by keeping your eyes on Him, not on clever arguments.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Here is the bedrock: in Christ dwells all the fullness of God—not a piece of divinity, not an intermediary, but the complete, embodied God. In Him, nothing is lacking, nothing hidden. This is Who you trust.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: You are made full in Him—filled, complete, lacking nothing that matters. And He is Head of all powers and principalities. Whatever unseen forces might trouble the world, He is over them. Your completeness comes from being under His headship.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: A circumcision not made with hands—your old self put off like an outgrown garment. Not a ritual on the flesh, but a real death to sin's dominion. Christ did this for you; now you belong to a different kingdom.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Baptism speaks this truth in water: buried with Christ, raised with Christ, through faith in His resurrection power. You went down into death's waters and came up on the far side of death—the God who raised Jesus reached down and raised you.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Dead in your trespasses, yet made alive together with Him. Not a change of scenery—a resurrection. And in that moment, He forgave all your trespasses, erasing the ledger of sin. That is grace: no record kept, no debt remaining.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The handwriting in ordinances that stood against you—the law that witnessed your guilt—He took it away and nailed it to the cross. Not by accident; by deliberate deed. Your condemnation is removed; the charge is satisfied.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The principalities and powers—the unseen forces that seemed so strong—He stripped them naked and led them in open triumph. In the cross, He won. Whatever evil tried to hold you is defeated. You are on the winning side.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Let no one judge you in eating or drinking, in feast days or new moons or Sabbaths. These are shadows—useful in their season, but they can't bind a conscience now that the substance, Christ, has come. Your freedom in Him is real.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: A shadow of things to come—but the things have come. Christ is the body that casts the shadow. When you know Him, you understand what the Law was always pointing toward. Rest there.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Some rob you with false humility and angel-worship, puffing themselves up with visions they claim to have seen. Pride masquerades as meekness; presumption hides as piety. Your prize is won by holding fast to Christ, not by grasping at spiritual experiences.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The Head supplies the whole body through joints and ligaments—all the connections that make us one, growing with God's growth. When you lose connection to Christ, you wither. Hold fast to Him; He holds the whole family together.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: If you died with Christ from the elements of the world—if you have truly shifted your citizenship—why do you live as if you still belong to this passing order? Ordinances and rules have no power over the dead. You are free.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The commandments of men: Don't handle, don't taste, don't touch. Rules stacked on rules, each one promising purity through abstinence. But they can't restrain the heart. Only Christ can.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: All these things perish with use—they are temporary, passing away. Yet they are the precepts and doctrines of men, given as if they were eternal truth. Hold them lightly. Hold Christ firmly.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Readers today hear an echo of this—in performance spirituality, in self-imposed disciplines that feel like depth but are only shadow. The appearance of wisdom and humility fills many hearts. Yet outward harshness to the flesh has no power to change the indulgence that hides inside. Only Christ can reach there. As of 2026-10, the old tricks still work on us; we still need reminding.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight
